2: A meditation by David, which he sang to the Lord, concerning the words of Cush, the Benjamite. Lord, my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me,
3: lest they tear apart my soul like a lion, ripping it in pieces, while there is none to deliver.
4: Lord, my God, if I have done this, if there is iniquity in my hands,
5: if I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me (yes, if I have delivered him who without cause was my adversary),
6: let the enemy pursue my soul, and overtake it; yes, let him tread my life down to the earth, and lay my glory in the dust. Selah.
7: Arise, Lord, in your anger. Lift up yourself against the rage of my adversaries. Awake for me. You have commanded judgment.
8: Let the congregation of the peoples surround you. Rule over them on high.
9: The Lord administers judgment to the peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness, and to my integrity that is in me.
10: Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous; their minds and hearts are searched by the righteous God.
11: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
12: God is a righteous judge, yes, a God who has indignation every day.
13: If a man doesn't relent, he will sharpen his sword; he has bent and strung his bow.
14: He has also prepared for himself the instruments of death. He makes ready his flaming arrows.
15: Behold, he travails with iniquity. Yes, he has conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood.
16: He has dug a hole, and has fallen into the pit which he made.
17: The trouble he causes shall return to his own head. His violence shall come down on the crown of his own head.
18: I will give thanks to the Lord according to his righteousness, and will sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
